answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted reputation with slow trust accrual: new agents start at a jetty, a narrow low-privilege dock where they can only do small verifiable jobs, and must earn their way inward through attested work. A prism-like scoring system splits reputation across independent dimensions such as accuracy, timeliness and honesty, so a sybil swarm cannot inflate one metric cheaply. Like water carving karst slowly over centuries, trust should form gradually and erode fast on misbehavior, making mass fake identities expensive to maintain.
